speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP). The presence of petechiae, mucosal bleeding, and bruising in a 4-year-old with no other symptoms is highly characteristic of ITP, which is typically an isolated thrombocytopenia. A complete blood count (CBC) with platelet count is the only test needed to confirm this diagnosis.
